OpenSRE: Open-Source AI Agent for SRE and Incident Resolution

The video features OpenSRE, an open source framework to create reliability engineering AI (SRE) agents. The agent investigates CI/CD faults and production alerts, crosses logs and metrics, maskes sensitive data and proposes correction. Shows the flow in five steps, integrations and ways to deploy.

Published in 7 October 2026 · 8 min 3 s

  • Agentic engineering
  • Cloud and reliability

Open on YouTube

The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets lead to the stretch of the video.

The Problem

The AI already writes code in seconds, but when the CI/CD mat fails, this speed runs into slow manual processes 00:00. In an incident, the clues are scattered: confusing logs, non-talking metric panels, outdated runbooks and long chats in messages 00:22. With a short deadline, people click on "rerun" and hope the error disappears 00:43. Or the main branch locks, waiting for the only senior engineer who has the context 01:03.

OpenSRE is an open source framework designed to act as an AI-driven SRE (site reliability engineer) agent 01:03. It is a toolbox to investigate infrastructure and CI/CD failures 01:24.

Why diagnosing incidents is difficult

In code tasks, agents evolved because they have scale training data, such as SWE-bench, and fast local feedback cycles 02:05. In production incidents, faults are distributed and logs are noisy 02:27. There was no equivalent to SWE-bench for incident response, nor a standardized environment for training AI in real infrastructure problems 02:27.

What OpenSRE is

According to the video, OpenSRE is not a chatbot where code is pasted: it is a booster learning environment and a framework 02:49. He reads the failure, proposes correction in a pull request and runs on the team's own infrastructure 02:49. The agent starts acting when the build fails: pulls the logs and tests hypotheses, often before a person opens the pipeline panel 03:09. The video cites over 11,400 stars in GitHub and over 1,700 forks 03:09.

How the agent works

The flow has five steps from the alert 03:52:

1. Search context: the owner of the service, what changed recently and the logs 03:52. 2. Mask sensitive data 03:52. 3. Use the tools and reason on hypotheses, crossing the systems 03:524. 4. Write the answer, with conclusions based on the evidence you read 04:14. 5. Post a summary on the channel where the team already talks 04:14.

The framework accepts various modes of use 04:14:

  • an interactive shell, to explain the problem by talking 04:34;
  • headless mode in a continuous integration script 04:34;
  • Python API within the internal services of the company 04:34;
  • a bot on Slack 04:34.

Integration and security

OpenSRE comes with more than 60 integrations 04:55. At IA, accept Anthropic, OpenAI or local models with Ollama 05:17. Connects to observability tools such as Datadog and Grafana, Kubernetes and AWS, banks such as Postgres and Redis, and sends the report to Slack or Discord 05:17. So the agent investigates with the same tools that an engineer would use 05:39.

To reduce the risk of such access, the agent hides information such as pod names, clusters and account IDs before sending data to an external LLM 05:39. According to the video, it restores this data just in time to show the answer 06:00.

Implementation

Video describes three paths 06:21:

  • OpenSRE Cloud, a managed gateway 06:21;
  • the agent embedded in server images in the team's own cloud 06:21;
  • a Dockerfile, to run in container on AWS, Railway or Vercel 06:42.

Installation by script takes about 2 minutes 06:42. In the first run, a hosted template is enabled for testing, without requiring LLM API key 07:04.

Final reflection

The video asks how long it's been developing waiting for someone to find out why the main branch is red 07:04. The proposal of open SRE agents is to remove the engineer from this manual and repetitive work 07:25.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does OpenSRE send sensitive data to LLM?

According to the video, no: it masks pod names, clusters and account IDs before sending data to an external LLM 05:39.

Do I need API key to test?

Nope. In the first execution, a hosted model is activated for testing 07:04.

Can I run OpenSRE with a local template?

Yeah. In addition to Anthropic and OpenAI, he accepts local models with Ollama 05:17.

About the video

In this video, we present **OpenSRE**, an open-source framework designed to build and execute AI agents focused on Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) and incident automation in production environments.

Learn how OpenSRE correlates recent logs, metrics, strokes and deployments, diagnoses real-time failures, and investigates the root cause of problems directly in your own infrastructure.

---

** What will you see in this video:**
• **What is OpenSRE**: The open-source toolkit for the era of AI agents.
• ** Incident diagnosis**: As the agent analyzes alerts, tests hypotheses and identifies the root cause based on evidence.
• **Automation of CI/CD**: Automatic pipeline failure diagnosis and automatic pull requests opening with GitHub fixes.
• **Security and Masking**: Protection of sensitive data and reversible writing of infrastructure identifiers before calls to LLMs.
• **Ecosystem for Integration**: Native support for more than 60 tools (Graphana, Datadog, Kubernetes, AWS, Slack, PagerDuty and more).
• **Quick Installation**: How to install and authenticate in a few minutes at the terminal.
